title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text: Every variable in your research has a level of measurement. The question type you choose decides what kind of data you get and which statistics you can run later.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Variables and question types
In research, a variable is any characteristic you measure or record for each participant, such as age, sex, or weight. Variables are divided into two main types:
Numerical variables are measured as numbers, and calculations such as mean or median.

Discrete: whole numbers that are counted, such as age in years or number of children.
Continuous: measurements that can have decimals, such as blood sugar, height, haemoglobin, and most other biomarker values.

Categorical variables place each participant into a group or category.

Nominal: categories with no natural order, such as sex, blood group, or hair color.
Ordinal: categories with a meaningful order, such as education level, pain severity, cancer stage, or a Likert scale.

Dates, times and free-text answers are also collected in surveys. The table below shows which question type to use in KoboToolbox for each type of variable.

TipMore question types and advanced features



XLSForm supports many more question types and options, such as repeat groups, file uploads, and cascading selects. For the full list with examples, visit the XLSForm question types reference.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Integer (whole number)
Used for counts and ages in completed years. No decimal point is allowed.

Poll: How many years have you worked as a nurse?


Examples: age in years, number of children, parity, number of hospital admissions, days of hospital stay.
Analysis: mean, median, SD, t-test, correlation.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Decimal
Used for measurements that need a fractional part.

Poll: What is your height in metres? (e.g. 1.62)


Examples: weight (kg), height (m), haemoglobin (g/dL), body temperature (°C), BMI.
Tip: always write the unit in the question.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Single option (select one)
The respondent can choose only one answer from a list.

Poll: In which inpatient department do you currently work? ☐ Medical ☐ Surgical ☐ Paediatric ☐ Maternity ☐ Critical care


Examples: sex, marital status, education level, yes/no questions.
Categories must not overlap, and must cover every possible answer (add “Other” if needed).

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Multiple option (select multiple)
The respondent can choose one or more answers.

Poll: Which sources do you use to learn about research methods? (select all that apply) ☐ Textbooks ☐ Journals ☐ YouTube ☐ Teachers ☐ AI tools


Examples: symptoms experienced, sources of health information, comorbidities.
In the data, each option becomes its own yes/no.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Date and time

Poll: On what date did you join the M.Sc. Nursing programme?
Poll: At what time does your morning duty usually start?


date: date of admission, date of delivery, last menstrual period.
time: time of medication, time of birth.
datetime: exact date and time of an event.
Digital forms use a date picker, so there are no confusing formats like 05/06/2026.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Text
Free, open-ended answers.

Poll: In one word, what is the biggest challenge in collecting thesis data?


Examples: “Other (please specify)”, suggestions, comments, qualitative answers.
Use text questions only when needed. They take longer to answer and are harder to analyse.

title: Module 1: Types of survey questions
text:
Note
A note shows information to the respondent or data collector but collects no answer.

Example: “This survey has 25 questions and takes about 10 minutes to complete. Your answers will be kept confidential.”


Use notes for introductions, section instructions, and thank-you messages.

title: Module 5: Create your KoboToolbox account (homework)
text:
ImportantComplete this before the in-person session



There is not enough time in class to wait for email confirmations.



Go to the KoboToolbox server:

Global server: https://kf.kobotoolbox.org

Click Create an account. 
Fill in your name, username, email and password. Use your real name and an email you check regularly.
Open the confirmation email and click the link to activate your account.
Log in and check that you see the Projects page.
Write down your username and the server you used. You will need them when setting up the KoboCollect app.

title: Module 6: KoboToolbox interface and uploading your XLSForm
text:
Click NEW → Upload an XLSForm.
Choose your .xlsx file and click Upload. 
Fill in project details (name, description, sector: Health, country: Nepal) → Create project.
If you see an error, read it carefully: it usually names the row and the problem (see the table below). Fix the Excel file and upload again via Replace form.
Click the eye icon (Preview) to test the form in your browser. Check skip logic, constraints and the language switch.
Click Deploy.

title: Module 6: KoboToolbox interface and uploading your XLSForm
text:
Collect test data

Web form: in the Form tab, open the Collect data section and choose the online-offline web form link. Open it on any browser or share it.
KoboCollect app (Android): install KoboCollect from the Play Store → configure the server with your server URL and username → Download form → Start new form. KoboCollect works offline in the field; send submissions when you are back online.
Submit 3 to 5 test records, including wrong values, to check your constraints.
In the Data tab, view the table and download the data as Excel. Check that each column is correct.







Warning



Delete all test submissions before you start real data collection.

title: Module 6: KoboToolbox interface and uploading your XLSForm
text:
Ethics and data protection

Collect only what your approved protocol needs. Avoid names and phone numbers unless required.
Share projects with your supervisor through Settings → Sharing rather than sharing your password.
Download and store data on a password-protected device.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
text: KoboCollect is a free Android app for collecting data with your KoboToolbox forms. Its biggest advantage is that it works offline: you can interview participants in places without internet, and send the data to the server later.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
text:
Step 1: Install KoboCollect

Open the Google Play Store on your Android phone.
Search for KoboCollect and install the app published by KoboToolbox.
Open the app.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
section: Step 2: Connect the app to your KoboToolbox account
text:
Step 2: Connect the app to your KoboToolbox account

When the app opens for the first time, choose Manually enter project details.
Enter the server URL:



Your account is on
Server URL for KoboCollect




Global server (kf.kobotoolbox.org)
https://kc.kobotoolbox.org



Enter your KoboToolbox username and password.
Save the settings. The app’s main menu appears.








Warning



The server URL for KoboCollect starts with kc, not kf. Using kf.kobotoolbox.org (the website address) is the most common setup mistake.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
section: Step 3: Download your form to the phone
text:
Step 3: Download your form to the phone

In the main menu, tap Download form.
Tick the form you deployed in KoboToolbox.
Tap Get selected.

If your form doesn’t appear, check that it is deployed (not only uploaded) in KoboToolbox, and that you entered the correct username and server.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
text:
Step 4: Fill in the form

Tap Start new form and choose your form.
Answer each question, and swipe left or tap Next to move forward.
To switch between English and Nepali, open the ⋮ menu at the top right and choose Change language.
At the end of the form, choose:

Finalize: the record is complete and ready to send.
Save as draft: you can open it later from Drafts and finish it.









Tip



Filling in forms does not need internet. You can complete many interviews offline during the day and send them all at once.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
section: Step 5: Send data to the server
text:
Step 5: Send data to the server

When you have internet, tap Ready to send in the main menu.
Select the records you want to send, or tap Select all.
Tap Send selected.
Sent records move to Sent. Check that they appear in the Data tab of your project in KoboToolbox.


To send records automatically whenever the phone is online, turn on Auto send in the app settings (under Form management).

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
section: Step 6: Update the form after changes
text:
Step 6: Update the form after changes
If you change your XLSForm and redeploy it in KoboToolbox, the phone still has the old version.

Send all finalized records first.
Tap Download form again and select the updated form.
Start new interviews with the new version.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
text:
Using an iPhone?
KoboCollect is only available for Android. On an iPhone, iPad or computer, use the web form instead:

In KoboToolbox, open your project’s Form tab and find the Collect data section.
Choose the online-offline web form option and copy the link.
Open the link in the browser and add it to the home screen.

The online-offline web form can also be filled in without internet once it has been opened, and it sends the data when the connection returns.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app
text:
Good practice in the field

Test before the field: fill in and send 3 to 5 test records, then check them in KoboToolbox. Delete the test records before real data collection.
Send data every day when possible. Records on the phone can be lost if it is damaged, stolen or reset.
Never uninstall KoboCollect or clear its data while records are still waiting in Drafts or Ready to send.
Protect the phone with a screen lock, since it contains participants’ data.
Carry a charger or power bank; long field days drain the battery.

title: Module 7: Collecting data with the KoboCollect mobile app

title: Module 4: XLSForm development with your research questions
text: Now build your own form. Work from your approved thesis questionnaire.

title: Module 4: XLSForm development with your research questions
text:
Step-by-step

Copy msn_xlsform_template.xlsx and rename it, e.g. lastname_survey_v1.xlsx. Keep the four metadata rows (start, end, today, deviceid) and replace the example rows with your own questions and answer options.
Settings sheet: write your form title (e.g. Dinesh HTN Research).
Consent first: add an introduction note and a required select_one yes_no consent question. Put the rest of the form in groups with relevant = ${consent} = 'yes'.
One group per section of your questionnaire (Section A, B, C …).
For each question, decide the type (use the Module 1 summary table), give it a short name, and copy the English label.
Add answer lists in choices. Reuse lists (e.g. one yes_no list for all yes/no questions).
Add rules: required, relevant for skip patterns, constraint for ranges.
Add Nepali labels in label::Nepali (ne) if you will interview in Nepali.
Save and upload it in Module 6 to test.

title: Module 7: Developing survey questions in the Kobo Formbuilder
text: KoboToolbox also has a point-and-click Formbuilder. It is useful for small forms and quick edits. XLSForm is better for long, bilingual thesis questionnaires, but it helps to know both.

title: Module 7: Developing survey questions in the Kobo Formbuilder
text:
Build a form from scratch

NEW → Build from scratch → enter project details → Create project.
Click + to add a question, type the question text, and choose the type (Select One, Select Many, Text, Number, Decimal, Date, Time, Note, Rating …).
For choice questions, type each option. Click + to add more options.
Click the gear icon (Settings) on a question to set:

Mandatory response (required)
Skip logic (relevant): choose the earlier question and condition
Validation criteria (constraint) and the error message
Appearance and hint

Select several questions and click Group to create a section.
Use Manage translations to add Nepali labels.
Save, Preview, then Deploy.

title: Module 7: Developing survey questions in the Kobo Formbuilder
text:
Formbuilder and XLSForm together

Download any Formbuilder project as XLS (Form tab → ⋯ → Download XLS). This is a good way to learn XLSForm syntax: build a question in the Formbuilder, download, and see how it is written.
You can upload an XLSForm and then make small edits in the Formbuilder.







NotePractice



Rebuild the Section C Likert scale from the example file in the Formbuilder using the Rating question type, then download it as XLS and compare it with the XLSForm version.

title: Digital Data Collection with XLSForm and KoboToolbox
text:
Many research studies in Nepal still collect data on paper and enter it manually into Excel or SPSS afterwards. This course shows you how to replace that process with digital data collection: you design your questionnaire once in an Excel file (an XLSForm), upload it to KoboToolbox, and collect data on a phone, tablet or web browser. Data arrive clean, coded and ready for analysis.
This self-paced course covers basic to semi-advanced skills. You can work through every module on this website to practice together and build your own research questionnaire in XLSForm. You will then upload it to KoboToolbox to collect data.






NoteWho is this course for?



This course is for students, beginner researchers, survey tool developers, and anyone who wants to move from paper questionnaires to digital data collection. The examples use health-related data. No programming knowledge is needed; basic computer and Excel skills are enough.




By the end of this course, you will be able to:

Choose the correct question type (integer, decimal, single choice, multiple choice, date/time, text, note, etc.) for each research variable.
Explain the sheets of an XLSForm (survey, choices, and settings) and create an XLSForm with a bilingual (English and Nepali) setup.
Convert your own questionnaire into an XLSForm, including required questions, groups, skip logic, and constraints.
Create a KoboToolbox account, upload and deploy an XLSForm, and collect test data.
Build and edit a survey directly in the KoboToolbox Formbuilder.
Download the KoboCollect app on a mobile device, link it to your KoboToolbox account, and use it to collect data offline and submit it to the server.
Download collected data from the KoboToolbox server in Excel, CSV, or SPSS format for analysis.





A laptop with Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc or Google Sheets
A smartphone with internet access
The KoboCollect app installed on an Android phone (see Module 7). iPhone users can use the web form instead.
A KoboToolbox account (see Module 5)
A copy of your research/thesis questionnaire (Word or PDF)
Download the course template: msn_xlsform_template.xlsx, an example template to start your own form

Using numbers 1–5 as choice names makes scoring easy.

To show all items as one grid instead, use table-list on begin_group (see Appearance in the tips below).







TipXLSForm tips and tricks





Most upload errors come from a few small mistakes. Check these before you upload your form.

The name column

No spaces. Use an underscore instead: marital_status, not marital status.
Start with a letter, not a number: q1_age, not 1_age.
Use only letters, numbers and underscores. No hyphens, dots, brackets or Nepali characters.
Every name must be unique in the survey sheet.
Keep names short and meaningful, in lowercase: hb_level is better than x7 or Haemoglobin_Level_Of_Patient.
Don’t rename a question after data collection starts. KoboToolbox treats the new name as a new question, and your data will be split into two columns.



The choices sheet

The list_name must match exactly the word after select_one or select_multiple in the survey sheet, including spelling and capital letters.
Choice names follow the same rules: no spaces, unique within the list.
Reuse lists. One yes_no list can serve every yes/no question.
For Likert scales, use numbers as choice names (1 to 5) to make scoring easy.
Add “Other” with a follow-up text question shown only when “Other” is selected.
Use fixed codes for special answers and keep them the same in every list, for example 98 = Don’t know, 99 = Refused.
Don’t change choice names after deployment. You can edit labels, but changing names makes old and new data inconsistent.



Skip logic and constraints

Refer to other questions as ${name}, spelled exactly as in the name column.
Put text values in single quotes (${consent} = 'yes'). Numbers don’t need quotes (${age} >= 18).
Use the choice name, not the label: 'yes', not 'Yes' or 'हो'.
For select_multiple, use selected(${symptoms}, 'fever'), not ${symptoms} = 'fever'.
In a constraint, . means the current answer: . >= 30 and . <= 80.
Write and / or in lowercase.
Always add a constraint_message, so the data collector knows what went wrong.



Structure

Sheet names must be exactly survey, choices and settings, in lowercase.
Column headers must be spelled exactly (constraint_message, not constraint message).
Every begin_group needs a matching end_group.
Don’t merge cells or use Excel formulas in the form.
Every question needs a label, except calculate rows and metadata (start, end, today, deviceid).



Multiple languages

Write language names identically in every column: label::Nepali (ne) everywhere, never Nepali (ne) in one column and nepali(ne) in another.
Fill in every language column for every question, including hints, constraint messages and choices.
Type Nepali in Unicode (Nepali Unicode keyboard). Preeti and other old fonts display as random letters on phones.
Set default_language in the settings sheet.



Appearance: change how a question looks
The appearance column changes how a question or group is displayed, without changing the data that are saved. Common appearances:








appearance
Use with
What it does




field-list
begin_group
Shows all questions of the group on one screen


table-list
begin_group
Shows questions with the same answer options as a grid


likert
select_one
Shows options in a row, like a rating scale


minimal
select_one / select_multiple
Shows options in a drop-down list, useful for long lists


multiline
text
Gives a larger box for long answers


month-year
date
Asks only for month and year, e.g. when the exact date isn’t known




More appearances Appearances can look slightly different in the web form and in KoboCollect, so always preview your form. For the full list with examples, see the XLSForm appearance reference.



Testing and versions
Check your form online before uploading XLSForm Online is a free tool from ODK that checks your XLSForm for errors, without needing a KoboToolbox account.

Go to https://getodk.org/xlsform/.
Click Choose file and select your .xlsx form.
Click Submit.
If there are errors, a message appears with the row number and the problem. Fix it in Excel, save, and submit again.
When the form has no errors, click Preview in browser to fill in the form as a respondent would, and test the skip logic, constraints and language switch.

XLSForm Online uses the same XLSForm rules as KoboToolbox, so most errors show up here first. Always do a final check in KoboToolbox before deploying, as a few display options can look slightly different there.

Preview the form in KoboToolbox before deploying, and test the skip logic, constraints and language switch.
Submit test data with wrong values on purpose, to check that your constraints work.
Increase the version in the settings sheet every time you change and re-upload the form.
Save each version with a new file name (survey_v1.xlsx, survey_v2.xlsx), so you can go back if something breaks.
Delete all test submissions before real data collection starts.







WarningExcel traps




Curly quotes: Excel may change 'yes' into ‘yes’, and KoboToolbox won’t accept curly quotes. In Windows Excel, turn this off under File → Options → Proofing → AutoCorrect Options → AutoFormat As You Type, and untick “Straight quotes with smart quotes”.
Extra spaces: a space at the end of a cell (sex) is invisible but breaks the link between list_name and select_one sex.
Automatic dates: Excel may turn entries like 1-5 into a date. Format those cells as Text before typing.









TipStuck on an error?



Read the error message carefully. It usually names the row number and the problem. Also check the course template: if your form works differently from the example, compare the two row by row.
